nodes.title: ATAC-Seq
nodes.scope: Illumina ATAC-Seq explanatory schematic and the explicitly cited adaptations, at the shared molecular-architecture level. The graph extracts the unbranched depicted route from native chromatin through Tn5 tagmentation and the combined DNA purification/amplification block to a DNA library. The initial assay overview and repeated "Open DNA" panel illustrate the same accessibility target, without a depicted chromatin-opening operation. Blue Tn5 icons bearing colored adapter marks are reagents; insertion and "Fragmented and primed" depict one coupled transformation. The drawing contains no cell-isolation, compartment-pooling, barcode-assignment or sequencing operation. Named adaptations are qualified in method_scopes rather than expanded into unshown workflows. The two single-cell references describe distinct implementations, not interchangeable names for the same cell-handling architecture. THS-seq is a cited comparator, not a depicted ATAC-seq variant.

original.label: Insert in regions of open chromatin → Fragmented and primed
original.description: Adapter-loaded Tn5 transposomes act on accessible portions of native chromatin DNA, simultaneously fragmenting it and inserting sequencing-adapter tags. original.mechanism: Tn5 transposase delivers its adapter payload to chromatin DNA. Steric hindrance makes transposition less probable in less accessible chromatin, so tagging is preferential rather than perfectly exclusive. The blue enzyme icon denotes the catalytic reagent; it is not an additional biological analyte or a separate workflow operation.
original.information_effect: Genomic sequence, insertion boundaries and distances between insertion events encode a sample of accessibility in the original chromatin. method_scopes.rationale: The card’s single-cell ATAC-seq citation is Cusanovich 2015, a distinct combinatorial cellular-indexing implementation. Adapter-loaded transposase tagging maps to op_tagment, using barcoded transposase complexes in this implementation. Populations of intact nuclei are first tagged, then intact nuclei are pooled and redistributed; nuclei are subsequently lysed and a second barcode is added by PCR. PCR products are pooled for sequencing. This preserves nucleus-to-fragment association through a combination of indexes, with possible barcode collisions. The main text supports PCR but does not establish a full match to the figure’s combined purification/amplification block, so op_library is not assigned wholesale.
